title: WeatherNext Cyclones: forecasting cyclones one day earlier
summary: Three-day forecasts match what earlier models achieved at two days: about 100 km trajectory error and 11 knots intensity error, compared with ECMWF-ENS and HWRF. The work is with the National Hurricane Center, CIRA, and the Met Office. The comparison uses historical 2023–2024 cyclones; why results are good at 28 km remains an open question.

evidence.tested: Historical cyclones from 2023-2024 were benchmarked deterministically and probabilistically against ECMWF-ENS (track) and HWRF (intensity): three-day errors matched earlier two-day forecasts; a 2025 storm is cited only as an anecdote.
evidence.unknown: Why the model is accurate at 28 km resolution is an open question; the 'extra day' is an average dependent on the chosen benchmarks, and the evaluation window is slightly unclear.
evidence.ai_role: A single model using Functional Generative Networks produced track, intensity and wind-structure ensembles of up to 1,000 members.
